newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIA - Don't ignore us on expansion.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIA - Don't ignore us on expansion.

text.p: Any expansion of NATO membership without taking Russian concerns into account could lead to "serious changes" in Moscow's foreign policy, Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov said on Friday.
He was outlining three possible outcomes of the West's determination to issue invitations to former Warsaw Pact members.
The worst option, Primakov told reporters, would be for NATO to pay no attention to Russian concerns, forcing Moscow to respond.
"Under these conditions we would be forced to think of very serious changes, including in the conduct of foreign relations," he said.
Primakov, who was speaking after addressing parliament behind closed doors, did not elaborate on what policy changes he had in mind.
The first option was that the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation would decide against accepting new members but Primakov said that this scenario "was not likely".
The second possibility was a serious effort by NATO members to consider Russia's concerns on the alliance's expansion -- which Russian officials say could threaten Moscow's security.
"It is to this end that we are striving," he said. "It is precisely because of this that we have started consultations and negotiations with NATO."

NATO expansion is expected to be a key topic at a planned summit meeting between Russian President Boris Yeltsin and U.S. President Bill Clinton. U.S. officials say it is expected to be held next month in Helsinki.
During talks with Yeltsin in Moscow last Sunday, French President Jacques Chirac also proposed a summit in France to discuss details of NATO's expansion.

Diplomats in Paris said that under the proposal, leaders of the United States, Russia, France, Germany and Britain would meet in April to establish the broad lines of a deal on future European security that could enable Moscow to accept the enlargement of NATO.
